persuasive-sales.name: Persuasive Sales
persuasive-sales.summary: Top-of-funnel sales arc that creates awareness and alignment with a prospective customer. Anchored in a market change, leading to your unique capabilities, supported by proof, ending with a clear call to action.

beats.name: Introduction
beats.description: Open with a brief framing of who you are and why this conversation is worth the prospect's next thirty minutes. Keep credentials short; the audience cares about their problem, not your résumé.

beats.name: Big Change
beats.description: Name the market shift the prospect's industry is living through. Make it concrete, recent, and undeniable. The change — not the product — is the reason they should care.

beats.name: Winners and Losers
beats.description: Show how the change is creating winners and losers in the prospect's space. Use named examples where you can. The goal is for the prospect to wonder which side they'll end up on.

beats.name: Benefits
beats.description: Paint the outcome a winner experiences: a vivid picture of the prospect's life on the other side of the change. Lead with what changes for them, not with what your product does.
beats.instructions: Describe benefits, paint a vivid picture

beats.name: Capabilities
beats.description: Reveal the unique capabilities that make those outcomes possible. Frame them as the 'magic gifts' the prospect needs to win the new game. Highlight what's structurally different from the alternatives.
beats.instructions: Present unique features as 'magic gifts' to the customer

beats.name: Evidence
beats.description: Share customer testimonials, case studies, and measurable outcomes from organizations like the prospect's. Pick evidence that maps to the benefits you promised, not generic logos.

beats.name: Call to Action
beats.description: Ask for the next step in the sales process. Be specific: a pilot, a workshop, a follow-on conversation with a named stakeholder. Make the smallest credible commitment that keeps momentum.

beats.name: Close
beats.description: Close with a final image and contact path. Leave the prospect with one line about why they're better off acting now than later, and clear instructions for how to engage.

general-public.name: General Public
general-public.summary: Mixed non-expert audience with no assumed domain knowledge.
general-public.description: A mixed audience of non-experts with no assumed domain knowledge. Prefer analogies to data, use only simple charts, set large text for accessibility, and structure the talk as a story. Keep chart density low; 10-15 slides.

media.name: Media & Press
media.summary: Journalists, analysts, and media professionals seeking newsworthy insights and quotable statistics.
media.description: Journalists, analysts, and media professionals looking for newsworthy insight and quotable statistics. Make headline numbers prominent, attribute every figure clearly, design for print, and add embargo notes when needed. Moderate chart density; 8-12 slides in press-kit format.

pitch.name: Pitch
pitch.summary: Present an opportunity and ask for investment, approval, partnership, or sponsorship.
pitch.description: Use when the deck needs to create interest and move a high-stakes audience toward backing the opportunity. Lead with the opportunity, prove credibility, and make the ask concrete.
pitch.outcome: The audience agrees to invest, sponsor, approve, or continue the conversation.
successCriteria: Ask and next step are explicit

conversational.name: Conversational
conversational.summary: Direct, dialog-style voice for podcasts, fireside chats, and small-group reviews.
conversational.description: Sound like one half of a real conversation. Ask questions on the slide and answer them; keep paragraphs short; lean into examples over abstractions. Useful when the deck is meant to support a discussion rather than to lecture.
voiceCues: Ask a question on the slide, then answer it on the next.
Use second person — speak to the room, not at it.
Lean on stories and concrete examples over abstract framing.
Keep each idea to one short paragraph; let the dialog do the rest.
avoid: Stuffing slides — leave room for the discussion.
Inside-baseball references the room may not share.
samplePhrases: Why now? Two things changed in the last six months.
Here's the part that surprised us — and what we did about it.
If you take one thing from this section, take this.

minimal.name: Minimal
minimal.description: A clean, minimalistic theme with a focus on simplicity and readability. Ideal for professional, straightforward presentations.

luxury.name: Luxury
luxury.summary: Muted metallic and deep tones for premium, high-stakes decks.
luxury.description: A restrained luxury palette with gold, terracotta, dark green, and blue-gray support for premium narratives.

cool-horizon.name: Cool Horizon
cool-horizon.summary: Cool blue-green palette tuned for professional business decks.
cool-horizon.description: A balanced cool-toned scheme with deep navy, business blues, and teal accents. It works well across strategy, finance, and technical narratives.

skeena.name: Skeena
skeena.description: Skeena is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Skeena Display for headings with Skeena for body text.

aptos.name: Aptos
aptos.description: Aptos is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Aptos Display for headings with Aptos for body text.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

table-beside.name: Table beside
table-beside.summary: A table with commentary beside it.
table-beside.description: Place a table beside its interpretation. Use the supporting text to explain the conclusion without repeating every cell.

timeline.name: Timeline
timeline.summary: Dated events or a roadmap along one axis, with optional notes.
timeline.description: Show events or milestones in chronological order. Label each item with a date or stage and a concise description.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
